fields.meta_title: Free Vehicle Inspection Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a vehicle inspection form drivers fill on a phone. A safety defect grounds the vehicle and alerts the shop, and reports land in your database.
fields.h1: Build a Vehicle Inspection Form That Sends Defects to the Shop
fields.hero_description: Describe your vehicles and what drivers check. Emergent builds the vehicle inspection form with photo fields and grounds any vehicle with a safety defect until the repair is signed.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Does With Each Defect
fields.features_subheading: A carbonless pad records the problem, then rides around in the cab. These six pieces get the report to whoever fixes the vehicle.
fields.feature_1:
A checklist that matches the vehicle

Pick the unit number and the form loads the items for that vehicle type. A box truck gets coupling devices and a liftgate check, while a pool sedan skips both and checks the spare.
fields.feature_2:
A photo on every failed item

Mark an item as failed and the form asks for a photo and a short note before it submits. The mechanic sees the cracked mirror or the worn tread before walking out to the lot.
fields.feature_3:
Safety defects ground the vehicle

Choose which failures ground a vehicle, such as a brake fault. The unit shows as out of service on the dispatch list and stays there until a mechanic records the repair.
fields.feature_4:
Repair sign-off on the same record

Let the mechanic open the report, note the part replaced and sign on a phone. The next driver reviews that sign-off before leaving, and the history stays on one record.
fields.feature_5:
Due dates for annual inspections

Store each vehicle's last periodic inspection and count down to the next one. The fleet manager hears about it a month ahead, and an overdue truck drops off the crew schedule.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your GitHub repository

Export the full codebase when you want to connect the form to telematics or a maintenance system. Your developers can host it on your own servers and keep building on it.
fields.why_title: Why Build Inspection Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: A printed pad holds the defect until somebody reads it. By then the truck may already be back on the road.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places a Defect Gets Caught
fields.tab_content_1:
A brake light out pulls truck 14 off tomorrow's run

After the last stop, a Northwind Movers driver files the post-trip report for truck 14 and marks a brake light out. Any lighting or brake defect sets the truck to out of service. A photo goes to the shop's Slack channel, and Dana, the shop lead, signs off the repair before dispatch can assign the truck again.
fields.tab_content_2:
Pickup and return photos sit side by side

Globex Car Rental photographs each side of a car when it leaves the lot and again when it comes back. At return, the agent's phone shows the pickup photo of each panel next to the new one. A dent on the rear bumper that was not there at pickup opens a damage report for the branch manager.
fields.tab_content_3:
Trade-ins over $500 in repairs wait for a manager

Every trade-in at Alder Auto Group gets a graded inspection before anyone prices it. On a 2019 sedan the technician marks brake pads and rotors at $420 and two rear tires at $310. The reconditioning estimate comes to $730, and anything over $500 goes to the used-car manager before the offer is made.
fields.tab_content_4:
Fleet manager emailed 30 days before a truck is due

Fernhill Landscaping needs a periodic inspection on each truck every 12 months. The form records the inspection and who did it, and the app counts down to the next one. Truck 6 is due in 30 days, and the fleet manager gets an email about it. Truck 3 is 4 days overdue and cannot go on a crew schedule.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Vehicle Inspection Form
fields.howto_description: Decide what grounds a vehicle and who clears it before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the parts your drivers check
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose when the form is filled
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the defects that ground a vehicle
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the items a regulator or your insurer asks about, then add what your own mechanics want to hear. A box truck and a pool sedan need different lists. Keep each item short enough to answer with pass or fail.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the moment the form is filled: before the first trip, after the last one, or at a handover such as a rental return. Each moment gets its own version, because each one answers a different question about the vehicle.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set the defects that keep a vehicle parked until a repair is signed, such as a brake fault or a bald tire. Everything else can be logged and scheduled for the next service visit without pulling the vehicle off the road.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the mechanic or shop lead who signs off repairs, plus a backup for nights and weekends. A grounded vehicle with nobody assigned to clear it sits in the yard for days while dispatch works around it.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your checklist and grounding rules into one prompt, with the name of whoever clears each repair. Emergent builds the inspection form, a vehicles table and a dispatch list that hides anything out of service. Change a rule later by asking.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add photos and the repair sign-off
fields.howto_step_6_des: Make the photo field required whenever an item fails, and give the mechanic a signature field. If you track annual inspections, store the last inspection date on each vehicle record with an email reminder ahead of the due date.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Walk out to a truck in the lot
fields.howto_step_7_des: Take a phone outside and file a test report with one failed item. Confirm the truck drops off the dispatch list and the alert arrives. Then sign off the repair and check that the truck comes back.

claims_to_source: Under 49 CFR 396.11, a driver prepares a written report at the end of each day's work covering parts such as service brakes, parking brake, steering, lighting, tires, horn, wipers, mirrors, coupling devices, wheels and rims, and emergency equipment
A property-carrying driver does not have to file a DVIR when no defect is found or reported
Before the vehicle runs again, the carrier repairs any listed defect that would affect safe operation, or certifies that repair is unnecessary, and keeps the DVIR for three months
Under 49 CFR 396.17 every commercial motor vehicle must pass a periodic inspection at least once every 12 months, and 396.21 keeps the record for 14 months
Under 49 CFR 396.13, before driving the driver must review the last vehicle inspection report and sign it when defects were noted and certified repaired
